findings.issue: The new 5xx logging branch at lines 143-148 runs before the X-Request-Id header, content-type and reply are set, and nothing guards it. When the converted cause is not an Error, it builds the trace with `String(cause)`. That call throws a TypeError for some objects: a null-prototype object (`Object.create(null)`), or an object whose `toString` or `Symbol.toPrimitive` throws. A scope callback, `persistStatus`, tenancy port, audit sink or store that throws such a value would make CommittedCommandResponseFilter.catch throw. No canonical envelope would be sent; the request would fall through to the platform's default error handling, which may be a non-canonical 500, a stack page outside production, or an unhandled rejection. Before this patch, the same input got the fixed envelope. The trigger is unusual, but this is a regression added by the observability change, and the item 27 contract says the public body and headers must stay exactly canonical.
findings.required_change: Make the logging branch unable to throw. Either wrap building the trace and calling COMMAND_LOGGER.error in try/catch that falls back to `exception.stack`, or build it without calling String() on arbitrary values (for example, `Object.prototype.toString.call(cause)` or `util.inspect(cause)` inside a try). Before the final gate, add an HTTP sensor where a callback throws `Object.create(null)` and assert the exact 500 envelope and header.

findings.issue: The new sensors assert two things about the log: the message contains `requestId=<X-Request-Id>`, and the trace contains the cause message. None of them asserts that the log message contains the public `errorCode`, which item 27 requires. The source does log it. The tenancy-port conversion keeps its cause in source (line 506) but has no logging sensor. Neither do the 5xx rejections that have no cause (module-required 503, marking-required, lock-timeout and ttl 500s). The store and COMMIT conversions to 503 are proven only indirectly, because they go through the same `reject` line as the audit sensor.
findings.required_change: Optional hardening before final: extend the logger assertions to also match `exception.errorCode` in the first argument. Add one logging sensor for the tenancy-port-failed path in transactional-command-provenance.integration.spec.ts and one for a no-cause 5xx rejection. After that, have the Architect rebind the trace.

summary: I found no blocking defects in the follow-up; it meets plan.md §Retomada item 27. I read the source and sensors; I did not rerun builds, tests, trace or api:baselines, so those results are the maestro's. `reject()` now takes an optional cause and puts it on the internal CommandRejectionResponse's HttpException `cause`. The scope-callback, tenancy-port, ctg5-callback (status, status-policy, response-not-json, audit-metadata) and setup/store/audit/commit 503 conversions all pass the original error. The filter uses a module-level Nest Logger to log every CommandRejectionResponse at 500 or above. The log message has the errorCode and the same requestId used for both X-Request-Id and the body. The trace is the cause's stack, or the rejection's own stack when there is no cause. The public body is still built only from canonical fields (statusCode, errorCode, message, requestId, optional details, retryable), so it never carries a cause or stack. The exact-envelope helpers plus `not.toContain(cause message)` prove this for 500 (scope, status-policy) and 503 (audit). Established behavior is preserved: StynxDataError and legacy data errors are rethrown before conversion. Consumer HttpExceptions (selectedHttpException) and handler-phase errors pass through unchanged. 409s (in-progress, mismatch) are not logged and are otherwise unchanged. The no-core module-required 503 keeps its envelope and now also logs its own stack. `reject`, CommandRejectionResponse and COMMAND_LOGGER are not exported, so the exported declaration surface should not change. That matches the reported 44/44 api:baselines, but I did not run it. The trace.json rebind only raises assertion counts (8→12 and 53→55) and adds one note. Existing assertions were wrapped in the logger spy, not removed, so no test is weakened. Two low-severity items remain before the consolidated final gate: `String(cause)` can throw inside the logging branch for a null-prototype object or one whose conversion throws, and the sensors do not cover the errorCode in the log, the tenancy-port path, or 5xx rejections without a cause. This review does not approve the final release.
